intro: Every few seconds, the XRP Ledger's validators agree on a new ledger, and sign it. This page doesn't take anyone's word for it. It checks every one of those signatures itself, right here in your browser, and prints a proof of what passed. Ink means it was checked here. Pencil means someone else said so.
key: It all starts with a single key. And that key isn't printed on the sheet. It's in the paper itself. Hold the sheet up to the light, and there it is. It belongs to the publisher of the validator list, and everything else on this proof is checked against it.
list: That key signed a list of validators: the servers the network relies on to agree. Your browser checks that signature before anything else, and then each validator's own key, vouching for the one it signs with today. Once all of that holds, the steps of the temple are inked.
sigs: Every validator on the list signs every ledger. When your browser has checked one of those signatures, that validator's column fills with ink. And below, its autograph is drawn from the very bytes of the signature. Watch them come in, one by one.
quorum: The rosette counts the signatures as they're checked. Once at least eighty percent of the validators have signed the same ledger, that's a quorum, and the network has accepted it. The roof goes on the temple, and the star on the foil seal is struck.
ledger: So what exactly did they sign? A fingerprint of the ledger, called a hash. Your browser computes that hash from the ledger's header itself, and compares the two. When they match, rays spread out from the dome, and the ledger's details are printed in the corner: its hash, its state root, when it closed, and how much XRP exists.
account: You can check any account, too. Look one up, and the relay's answer is written in pencil first. Then your browser follows that account's path through the ledger's state tree, hashing every step up to the state root. Only if it all matches is the balance inked, and the lantern on the dome lights up. Try the genesis account: the very first account the ledger ever had.
closer: There's more to find if you look closer. Under ultraviolet light, the names of this ledger's signers glow around the temple. Zoom in anywhere, or take out the loupe to read the microprint in the border. And turn the sheet over for a checklist of every step, ticked off for this ledger. Everything you've seen here was checked by your own browser.
